preregistration.expectation: Rerun the synthetic ai-memory comparison with the embedding opt-out (AI_MEMORY_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=none) inside `unshare -rn` (a fresh network namespace with only `lo`, brought up manually, and no other network device), against a disposable data dir on an alternate port, with AI_MEMORY_SERVER_URL pointed at that alternate port. Because the namespace has no non-loopback device at all, the live ai-memory.service on the host's default port is also unreachable from inside it, independently forcing correct isolation (unlike gap 11's incident, which relied only on a port change). Expect either a measured zero external-network-byte delta, or -- if any non-lo interface exists in the namespace -- a zero byte delta on it during the writes.
preregistration.criteria: As written after the run: a byte count around the opt-out path. Settling the gap needs both next_check arms and a probe that can detect an attempted egress.

results: Advanced, not settled. What the raw output shows: inside `unshare -rn`, with lo the only interface, a disposable instance with AI_MEMORY_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=none served on 127.0.0.1:49590 and completed init, status and write-page with no network device; /proc/net/dev moved from 0 to 3299 bytes on lo across status plus write-page. What it cannot show: whether the opt-out path still attempts egress. In a namespace without a route, a connect() to any non-loopback address fails (ENETUNREACH) before any byte is counted, so /proc/net/dev cannot detect an attempted download, which was the original problem. Only the last 30 serve.log lines were captured, so the log does not rule out an attempt either. Remaining: (1) the next_check's separate arm, a /proc/net/dev or nethogs byte delta with a real network device present, or `strace -f -e trace=connect` evidence that no non-loopback connect is attempted; (2) the full synthetic comparison sequence rather than init/serve/status/write-page.
limits: Detection method: /proc/net/dev byte counters inside a device-less namespace. They can show that no non-loopback bytes were sent, but cannot detect a failed connection attempt.
Only one write-page (plus two status calls) was exercised, not the synthetic comparison.
The live-store status reads were CLI calls to the live service; read-only, but a rule break.
Disposable data dir and serve process were removed afterwards (transcript calls [13], [29], [51]).
